transcript: Alright, New York theatre fans, listen up. This is a time-sensitive roundup of shows closing in December or early January. This is not comprehensive. I'm including shows that I already saw, or shows that I hope to see in December. Now, there was something like seven shows from my November video that have now extended into December. So I'm gonna start by shouting out those starting off with Initiative A five hour coming of age play, with a D&D component. I found it quite beautiful. The experience was like binging a really well written mini series, but live! also at the Public, The seat of our pants, a kooky, and in my opinion, endearingly messy musical adaptation of The Skin of Our Teeth, with a great cast of Broadway stars. You got the Burning Cauldron of Fiery Fire, A very strange, enigmatic play by Anne Washburn about people living on a commune separated from the rest of society. I found it to be a bit of a tough nut to crack, but deeply absorbing nonetheless. Queens is a moving drama about a group of immigrant women living together in a basement apartment. And again, the cast here is pretty extraordinary. Prince F has announced its final extension. It's proven to be a pretty big hit and in my opinion, deservedly so. Obviously the premise for this one has been controversial, but I think they handled it beautifully. Okay, I don't wanna say too much about Practice, if you haven't seen It. But it's sort of about an experimental theatre troupe and I've been telling all my friends to run and see this. I've heard very good things about Meet the Cartozians, which appears to be a multi generational historical fiction dramedy? Michael Urie is starring in a production of Shakespeare's Richard II with a queer 1980s spin and a really clever framing device that fit nicely with the text. We've got the F*gg*ts and their friends Between Revolutions, which appears to be an interpretative adaptation of Larry Mitchell's 1977 gay manifesto book of the same name. Some of my favorite actors in New York are starring in this play Everything is Here about a group of people in a retirement community acting out scenes from A Streetcar Named Desire. One of the big hits of the fall season, Weer is finally closing after multiple extensions. It's this wild, unhinged parody of Y2K romcoms by Natalie Palamides, where she plays both people in a couple, one with each half of her body. This is a Pride and Prejudice adaptation that is still a period piece, but written with a fresh, contemporary feel. What if they ate the baby? Is a kind of surreal, dark comedy from the clown duo Xhloe and Natasha. It's sort of a play on 1950s housewives. The comedy is extremely sharp here, but it also goes to some tragic places. A revival of Gruesome Playground Injuries, starring Kara Young and Nicholas Braun. This was actually my first time seeing this play, and I found it quite touching. Both actors are very strong, but Kara Young is one of my faves. She's excellent as ever. This might be my favorite performance of hers I've seen in a while.
